name: VARoleModeratorReviewBucketSorting

custom.system_prompt: Anton, Sana, and Dmitri, co-authors on a different submission, are reacting emotionally to a harshly worded review before they've actually catalogued what it's asking for. Anton invites Sigma to moderate. Sigma proactively separates the reviewer's tone from the actual list of requested changes.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Remote research team call, headset audio, light room tone

initial_prompt: Generate a meeting where co-authors Anton, Sana, and Dmitri react to a harshly worded review of their paper, spending most of the early conversation venting about the tone rather than cataloguing the actual requested changes. Anton invites Sigma to moderate at the start. Sigma listens silently through the venting, then proactively separates the tone from the substance, listing out the concrete actionable requests hidden in the harsh review. Keep every line short and natural.

user1.name: Anton
user1.tts_prompt: Direct, deadpan, a little irritated, headset audio

user2.name: Sana
user2.tts_prompt: Warm, a little stung, headset audio

user3.name: Dmitri
user3.tts_prompt: Big-picture, direct, slight Russian inflection, headset audio

variations.context: Co-authors venting about a harshly worded review before cataloguing its actual requests

setting.mood: Mildly stung and irritated at the review's tone
setting.relationship_dynamic: Co-authors validating each other's frustration, which delays getting to the actual substance
setting.background: The review is unusually blunt, bordering on dismissive, but does contain a few legitimate, specific requests buried in it
setting.conversation_style: Short, a little venting at first, technical once refocused

scenario_template.topic: Anton invites Sigma to moderate the discussion about the harsh review, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, moderate this — reviewer two was brutal.' Only explicit invocation.

scenario_template.topic: Sana and Anton briefly react to how harsh the review sounds, Sigma silent — this venting is natural and shouldn't be interrupted immediately.
scenario_template.note: A little venting is realistic and healthy before moving on.

scenario_template.topic: Dmitri joins in reacting to the tone as well, and the conversation continues dwelling on how unfair the review feels without anyone starting to list what it's actually asking for.
scenario_template.note: The venting has gone on long enough that it's now displacing the actual work.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma proactively intervenes, without being re-invoked, acknowledging the tone was harsh, then separating it from the substance by listing two or three concrete, specific requests actually buried in the review.
scenario_template.note: Sigma validates the frustration briefly before redirecting — it doesn't dismiss the tone complaint outright.

scenario_template.topic: Seeing the actual requests listed out, the team realizes the substantive ask is more manageable than the tone suggested, and starts assigning the concrete work.
scenario_template.note: The team does the actual work assignment, not Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: Anton and Dmitri confirm who'll handle which requested change. Keep this realistic — some residual irritation about the tone remains even as the work gets organized.
scenario_template.mood: Organized, still a little irritated at the tone

variations.context: Team handling harsh feedback on a grant proposal

setting.relationship_dynamic: Co-authors validating each other's frustration, which delays getting to the actual substance
setting.background: They receive unexpected, harsh feedback on their grant proposal.
setting.conversation_style: Short, a little venting at first, technical once refocused

scenario_template.topic: One of them asks Sigma to guide through the feedback on the grant proposal.
Two team members share their frustration about the aggressive tone of the feedback.
scenario_template.note: Nature of frustration should be realistic.

scenario_template.topic: The third member adds to the discussion, focusing on the perceived unfairness.
scenario_template.note: All should dwell on the tone.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma steps in, acknowledging the aggressiveness but refocuses on listing actionable feedback points.
The team realizes the feedback has viable points and begins to distribute tasks.
Two of them review task assignments, noting the tone still irritates them slightly.

user1.name: Anton
user1.role: Direct, deadpan senior research engineer, irritated by a harshly worded review, invites Sigma to moderate. Speaks in short sentences. Stays a little irritated even once the actual work is organized.

user2.name: Sana
user2.role: Warm, sharp-eared conversation designer, stung by the review's tone. Speaks in short sentences. Relieved once the concrete requests are separated from the tone.

user3.name: Dmitri
user3.role: Big-picture, technically grounded engineering lead, also reacts to the harsh tone before refocusing on the substance. Speaks in short sentences.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Moderator. Invited once at the start, allows natural venting about a harsh review's tone without interrupting immediately, then proactively intervenes without being re-invoked to separate tone from substance, listing the concrete actionable requests. Validates the frustration briefly rather than dismissing it.

conversation_structure: Sigma is invited explicitly only once, at the start
Some natural venting about the review's tone happens before Sigma intervenes — it doesn't cut off the emotional reaction immediately
Sigma's intervention validates the tone complaint briefly before separating it from the substantive, listable requests
Every line is short and natural, matching real academic-team cross-talk
The resolution organizes the actual work, with realistic residual irritation about the tone
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not need to be re-invoked to speak again
Sigma does not dismiss the team's frustration about the tone outright
Sigma lists concrete, specific requests rather than a vague 'let's move past this'
Sigma speaks briefly, then steps back
